{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZjx0gg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDKehg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 87, "title": "Resolve and correct SPC700 readback at $F0/$F1/$FA–$FC", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `b98759ae45df6234f43d01511af6c12073a12710`, `Apu::read` returns backing RAM for TEST `$F0`, CONTROL `$F1`, and timer targets `$FA–$FC`. `Apu::write` stores written values at these addresses, making them readable as RAM. Timer counting also consumes the stored target bytes, so correcting reads must preserve target writes and timer behavior. See [read/write dispatch and target comparison](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/b98759ae45df6234f43d01511af6c12073a12710/crates/snes-core/src/apu.rs#L146).

The latest assessment specifically identifies this gap. Existing [timer tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/b98759ae45df6234f43d01511af6c12073a12710/crates/snes-core/tests/spc_timers.rs) exercise target writes, output reads and CONTROL effects, but do not establish readback for these five addresses. [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/b98759ae45df6234f43d01511af6c12073a12710/README.md#L535) explicitly leaves register readback unresolved. No supplied open Issue duplicates this work.

## Expected outcome

Implement the attributed ordinary SPC700 readback rules for these five addresses, independently of backing RAM, while preserving supported write effects.

The candidate contract requiring specification confirmation is:

| Address | Register | Candidate ordinary read behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$00F0` | TEST | Return `$00`, independent of the backing byte |
| `$00F1` | CONTROL | Return `$00`, independent of the last CONTROL write |
| `$00FA–$00FC` | Timer targets | Return `$00`, while target writes remain effective |

A read must not perform a write, clear timer output, restart a prescaler, change counting stages or clear communication ports. These restrictions must also be attributed before becoming hardware assertions.

**Evidence prerequisite:** the repository's validation documents cite hardware references but do not reproduce these readback passages. This planning pass inspected only repository material and supplied context; the zero-valued contract is therefore provisional. Before production edits, inspect the relevant entries in [Anomie's SPC700 Doc, revision 1126](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/spc700.txt), under **SPC700 REGISTERS**, and [Fullsnes, SNES APU SPC700 I/O Ports](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesapuspc700ioports). Record the revision, per-register statements and any disagreement. A write-only label alone does not establish the returned value. Correct any contradicted candidate requirement before implementing or freezing tests; explicitly retain unresolved behavior rather than inventing an electrical value.

Preserve the independently attributed timer contract from [Issue #85 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/b98759ae45df6234f43d01511af6c12073a12710/docs/issue-85-validation.md): free-running prescalers, enable-gated counting, rising-enable clearing of counting/output stages only, eight-bit post-increment live-target equality, and read-cleared four-bit outputs. This Issue does not reopen those rules without contrary evidence.

## Context and reproduction

Static reproduction of the current implementation:

```rust
let mut apu = snes_core::apu::Apu::default();
apu.write(0xf1, 0x07);
assert_eq!(apu.read(0xf1), 0x07);
apu.write(0xfa, 0x35);
assert_eq!(apu.read(0xfa), 0x35);
```

These results follow directly from the inspected dispatch; this planner did not execute tests. Nonzero backing bytes likewise distinguish the current TEST and other target reads from the candidate contract. Fresh zero-initialized instances alone cannot detect the gap.

Scope is ordinary, noncoincident SPC700 register reads through `Apu::read` and executing SPC instructions. Preserve writable state even when its CPU-facing readback differs. Avoid unrelated storage refactoring.

Non-goals and remaining SPC work include TEST clock/RAM-control implementation, physical bus-access and coincident timer edges, communication races, reset retention, SLEEP/STOP distinctions, comprehensive instruction coverage, IPL execution and DSP subcycles. Neighboring registers are regression controls, not an expansion into their complete hardware semantics.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Establish and document the per-register hardware contract using the sources above before production edits. Distinguish documented facts, derived expectations, fixture conventions and unresolved uncertainty. Do not use another emulator's output as the oracle. Implement demonstrated mismatches; documentation alone does not complete a supported readback correction.
- [ ] Add original MIT Rust tests, preferably in `crates/snes-core/tests/spc_io_readback.rs`, covering every selected address with distinct nonzero backing sentinels, repeated reads, and zero/nonzero register writes where their documented effects permit them. Assert explicit source-derived values independently of the implementation. Record at least one behavioral failure against the exact baseline for each corrected register class, followed by passes on the implementation.
- [ ] Prove that selected-register reads preserve timer phase, live targets, counting and accumulated output. Use all three timers, separated observation windows and independently calculated expected outputs. Retain all 11 existing `spc_timers` tests and their original numeric guest records without weakening assertions.
- [ ] Cover neighboring routing: `$F2/$F3` DSP address/data, `$F4–$F7` independent input/output directions, `$F8/$F9` storage, `$FD–$FF` read-to-clear outputs, and ordinary RAM outside the I/O page. Include `$01F0/$01F1/$01FA–$01FC` RAM controls and an executing direct-page selection control so decoding does not accidentally affect page 1.
- [ ] Add an original firmware-free uploaded SPC700 guest that reads all five selected addresses and distinguishing neighboring controls, records actual results outside the I/O page, and publishes a completion marker within a fixed master-clock budget. Use distinct backing sentinels as fixture inputs, never injected expected results. Avoid undocumented TEST writes or clock-mode changes. Derive expected records independently; require them separately in whole and irregularly partitioned runs before comparing determinism, PCM, DSP registers and relevant machine state. Bound upload polling and guest execution.
- [ ] Document original authorship, MIT licensing and generated guest provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`. Update README and a focused validation record with actual commands/results and remaining limitations. Preserve existing source pins, game hashes, licensing decisions and regression assertions.
- [ ] Pass the focused suite, existing timer tests, APU cadence tests and workspace checks:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test spc_io_readback
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test spc_timers
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib apu::timing_tests
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
```

- [ ] Pass the existing source-built hardware and browser gates from [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/b98759ae45df6234f43d01511af6c12073a12710/README.md#L74), using its documented toolchain prerequisites:

```sh
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Preserve Castle progression, Memory gameplay/music/effects, freeze detection, Web Audio and queue/drift assertions. Use only original tests or the existing licensed source-built fixtures described in [PROVENANCE](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/b98759ae45df6234f43d01511af6c12073a12710/tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md) and [CLEARED-GAMES](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/b98759ae45df6234f43d01511af6c12073a12710/tests/roms/CLEARED-GAMES.md). No commercial ROM or firmware acquisition is required.

- [ ] Retain the supplied inventory and every category's full scope and outstanding qualifications. `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo` and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `ppu-raster` and `pal` remain unimplemented. This bounded correction does not verify a category, establish commercial compatibility or complete Issue #3.

## Optional validation

None. Physical-device evidence may resolve a disputed specification but is not mandatory for an otherwise documented ordinary readback correction.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
